title: SOH-CAH-TOA
examples: When do I use trigonometry in real life?
What does the 'SOH' actually stand for?
Can I use this if the triangle is not a right triangle?

explain.say: Today we learn about trigonometry in right triangles. We use special ratios to find unknown sides or angles. Remember these ratios help us relate angles to side lengths.
First we must correctly label the sides of our right triangle. We always start from the angle we know or want to find. The hypotenuse is always the longest side opposite the right angle.

Next we learn the mnemonic SOH CAH TOA. SOH means sine of an angle equals opposite divided by hypotenuse. CAH means cosine equals adjacent divided by hypotenuse. TOA means tangent equals opposite divided by adjacent.

draw.text: sin = opp/hyp, cos = adj/hyp, tan = opp/adj

explain.say: Let us try an example together. If the opposite side is five and the hypotenuse is ten, we find the sine. Sine is opposite divided by hypotenuse, so sin equals five divided by ten.

faq.q: What is the hypotenuse always opposite?
faq.a: The hypotenuse is always the side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side in the triangle.

faq.q: When do I use the tangent ratio?
faq.a: You use tangent when you know the opposite side and the adjacent side. It relates these two sides to the angle.

faq.q: Does the angle I choose matter for SOH CAH TOA?
faq.a: Yes, the angle you choose determines which sides are opposite and which are adjacent. Always label relative to that angle.
asks: Do I have to pick the smaller angle?
How does the angle change the ratios?

faq.q: If I know two sides, how do I find the angle?
faq.a: You use the inverse trigonometric functions like arcsin or cos inverse. You find the ratio of the known sides first.
asks: How do I find the angle from sides?
What is the inverse of sine?

faq.q: Can I use these ratios if the triangle is not a right triangle?
faq.a: No, SOH CAH TOA only works for right-angled triangles. You need the right angle to define the sides properly.
asks: Does this work for general triangles?
What if there is no 90 degrees?

facts: SOH stands for sine equals opposite divided by hypotenuse.
CAH stands for cosine equals adjacent divided by hypotenuse.
TOA stands for tangent equals opposite divided by adjacent.
The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle.
Trigonometry ratios only apply to right-angled triangles.

quiz.say: In a right triangle, the side across from the angle is called:
quiz.why: The side directly across from the angle you are considering is called the opposite side. The hypotenuse is always the longest side, and adjacent is the side next to the angle.

wrong.1: Hypotenuse is always the side opposite the right angle, not the angle in question.
wrong.2: Adjacent is the side next to the angle, not the side across from it.
wrong.3: Leg is a general term, but 'opposite' is the precise term for the side across.

quiz.say: If the adjacent side is 8 and the hypotenuse is 10, what is the cosine of the angle?
quiz.why: Cosine is adjacent divided by hypotenuse. So, it is 8 divided by 10. You cannot use the hypotenuse divided by the adjacent side.

wrong.1: This incorrectly swaps the adjacent and hypotenuse roles.
wrong.2: You should not square the ratio when calculating the cosine.
wrong.3: This would only be true if the adjacent side was equal to the hypotenuse.

quiz.say: Which ratio relates the opposite side to the adjacent side?
quiz.why: The ratio that uses the opposite and adjacent sides is the tangent. Sine uses the hypotenuse, and cosine also uses the hypotenuse.

wrong.0: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine, not the ratio of opposite to adjacent.
wrong.2: Sine always involves the hypotenuse in its ratio.
wrong.3: Cosine also always involves the hypotenuse in its ratio.
